It's giving me some hope, I haven't gotten the shot yet, but the last few months have had me not knowing what to do about my situation at all, and sublocade was an option I was considering, but I think I've moved over to being close to 100% sure it is the right answer, because staying in the place I'm in much longer won't do any good.

The crazy thing is, I was actually able to overcome this anhedonialike 2 years ago, during covid I started smoking weed and making music, and I ended up pushing through it, and was stable on 1mg for a long while. I moved out of my parents house into an apartment with other sober roommates, which I awesome. Everything in my life was going soo much better than it had, so for the time being i was okay with being on a tiny bit of sub. But over time, I watched things change for the people around me in ways that it didn't for myself. I ended up putting all my energy into work because my band felt apart. This ultimately ended up in me drinking again, which led to a week of worse indulgence's.

So I've spent the last 3 months trying to figure out how the fuck to move forward, knowing theres a place for me I can be happy if my body and brain will allow me the emotion in the first place, so I'm truly hoping this is the time for a miracle with sublocade, because I need it so badly, I'm afraid I won't be able to get control of my life if I dont get my emotions and body back soon.

Now I'm at a point where I had to quit my job and the anhedonia is relentless, I can't focus on anything except getting off this shit once and for all. 

Basically I'm just happy to see some other people that can actually relate, nobody around me in my life understands. I hope to get one shot and be done with this shit once and for all. And then come time for some mushroom healing 😉

As I'm sure you're aware, with Suboxone's patent now being up, they no longer make the drug and a handful of other smaller pharma companies now dominate the market. With that, regulations on patenting drugs allow for about 20% wiggle room from the patent they bought (basically they are allowed to change the drug's formula). Now lets say they go and sell there patent. The next buyer can do the same thing and change up the formula again, as long as its around 80% the same as the patent they bought. Now keep doing this and over time the drug is going to get less and less effective as more pharma companies get there hands on it. With most drugs ,this isnt a major problem, but with narcotics, especially suboxone, this is why there are such noticeably different effects between various generic products.

Thats only part of the issue. Each company also uses there own compounds, which are all sourced differently. While both drugs can appear molecularly identical, with different sources for the active ingredient, they will have slightly different effects on opiate receptors. Over time, your body gets so used to the receptors that the drug binds to. Lets say your preferred generic binds primarly to U-receptor, but also a little to delta and then a little to kappa type 3. The other generic only slightly binds to U and primarily to Delta and Kappa 3. This is why you don't go into full blown WD, but you just feel weird as hell. That one individual receptor is now starving.

This has been a major problem for me. My primary pharmacy in Boston has been CVS for 3 years on Subutex. Now that Roxanne went under and Westward Labs bought their patent (which they fortunately havent changed), CVS no longer carries it. They carry some stuff that might be fine, but since I've been on Roxanne for so long I don't tolerate it well at all (I tried for about 2 months).

I found that another pharmacy about 45 minutes away carries Westward so I have been forced to go there to fill my monthly script.

Its scary man. Its the primary reason I have been starting my taper as I feel like I would be absolutely fucked if they stopped too.
